RFP# 97: FY202 4 National School Lunch Program Equipment Assistance Grant  
for School Food Authorities  
 
Questions & Answers  Summary  
General  
 
1. The way we read the paperwork  is that there should only be one contact with the SharePoint  link, 
(only one duly authorized user) to upload all the submissions. We understand that you don't want 
multiple submissions from one district, but if it is allowable for our district to have another email 
on file, my email would make more sense, as I will be writing and submitting the grant ap plications.  
 
Answer:  It is recommended that each SFA interested in applying appoint one individual to 
submit information to SharePoint. All food service directors, business officials, and Child 
Nutrition fiscal contacts entered in the Child Nutrition Management System (CNMS) as a 
contact for an NSLP -participating eligible SFA have been sent an email invitation to gain access 
to the SharePoint site.  
 
If an SFA would like a n additional  person  to have access to SharePoint other than the one(s) 
who received the invitation, a request  can be sent to RFP97@nysed.gov  . The email request 
must contain the SFA name, SFA LEA code, the individual’s  name, title, and the email  address 
that should be granted access to the SharePoint site. Invitation requests for SharePoint will be 
accepted and approved until 4:00 p.m. June 16, 2025. Requests to access SharePoint after this 
time will not be granted . 
  
2. Can you clarify what is meant by “SFAs must obligate their full grant funding by no later than 
9/30/2025” in the RFP? 
 
Answer:  USDA guidance requires all awarded SFAs to fully obligate their grant award  by 
September 30, 2025 . To meet this requirement, SFAs must  commit to purchasing the awarded 
item from a properly procured vendor.  All procurement , installation , and expenditure 
activities must be completed by  the projected end date of  6/30/26.  
 
3. The only number we do not have access to here is the OSC Vendor ID – would you be able to 
provide me a contact or information so I could obtain such number to continue through the 
process?  
 
Answer:  OSC Vendor IDs can be located by logging into the Child Nutrition Management 
System (CNMS) and navigating to the School Food Authority General Information page.  
 
Application  
4. Where is the actual application for this grant?   
 
Answer:  The grant application has been posted as a fillable PDF attachment with the RFP and 
can be found here . Please scroll down to the bottom of the page.  
 

2 
 5. We have two ideas for proposals. Can we submit more than one proposal? Will only one 
proposal per applicant be awarded?  
 
Answer:  Eligible applicants can submit more than one application if they would like. When 
considering this , please keep in mind  that an RA may be awarded more than one application  
request ; however, total combined awards to an SFA for an individual RA cannot exceed 
$20,000. Please see the Method of Award section of the RFP for more information.  
 
6. Is this something that you can help me write  or is there  another grant writer I should use?   
 
Answer:  The Office of Child Nutrition administers this grant funding but is not able to provide 
any information that would give an advantage to one applicant over another. Applicants may 
use the assistance of grant writers if they would like ; however, this is not required,  and the 
office does not make recommendations for specific writers or organizations.  
 
7. Can you please clarify if the RFP must be signed by the District Superintendent or by the FSA?  
 
Answer:  The certification must be signed by the SFA’s Chief School/Administrative Officer for 
the application to be considered. The Food Service Director may not sign the written 
certification.  
 
The following administrators are authorized to sign the certification: in cases of public schools 
– the Superintendent of the school district or their duly authorized designee; in cases of not -
for-profit corporations operating recognized non -public schools  or in cases of public or private 
non-profit residential childcare institutions – the officer of the corporation (e.g. Executive 
Director or their duly authorized designee); and in cases of charter schools – the chief school 
officer, administrator , or thei r duly authorized designee.  
 
8. Is it a $20k maximum  for the district or $20k per building if I apply for each building separately ? 
 
Answer:  The $20,000 maximum applies to each eligible RA under a n SFA. The total award an 
SFA receives may add up to more than $20,000 ; however, no individual RA will rec eive an 
award greater than $20,000.  
 
9. While trying to compile quotes for the Equipment Assistance Grant, I am getting some feedback 
from the vendors about the “potential price changes to pricing”, due to any tariffs that may 
come down at the last minute. They are trying to speculate the prices . What happens if they bid 
lower than the actual price at the time of the purchase? Will the school need to pay the 
difference?  
 
Answer:  Quotes submitted  as part of the appli cation process are used to  substantiate the 
cost of the item applied for. Awards will be made for specific equipment items for specific 
award amounts based on the application request. When making purchases of awarded 
equipment items, SFAs must follow proper procurement. Reimbursement will be paid to the 
SFA for the cost of the awarded item up to  the amount awarded ; however,  any expense 
greater than the award ed amount  will need to be covered by the SFA.  
 

3 
 10. Last year, mandatory requirements were included in the RFP for non -public schools (which 
stated non -public schools were required to submit a copy of their certificate of occupancy, as 
well as a current fire inspection with no violations ), but I don't see those in this year's RFP . I 
wanted to confirm that we do not need to upload these for this year's RFP .  
 
Answer:  Correct. There is no mandatory requirement for non -public RAs to submit a 
certificate of occupancy or a building fire inspection showing no violations, when applying 
for the RFP 97 FY24 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant for SFAs. Please see the RFP for more  
detail on eligibility and application requirements.  
 
Eligibility  
 
11. If we receive an invitation, does it mean that we can apply?  
 
Answer:  Receiving an invitation to  the SharePoint  submission site  does not guarantee 
eligibility. Individuals who request an invitation to apply for this grant during the listed 
application period will be provided one. Please refer to the posted RFP and Previous Food 
Service Equipment Grant Recipients  list prior to completing an application submission , as 
applications for ineligible SFAs/RAs will not be considered for review or award.  
 
12. I am reaching out because we were a recipient of the equipment grant last year and I was 
wondering how long we have to wait to apply for another one ? Our walk -in cooler/freezer is slowly 
showing signs of needing replacing and I wasn’t sure if we could apply again for next year.  
 
Answer:  The availability of funding  and the eligibility requirements to apply for this grant differ 
from year to year. It cannot be guaranteed at this time if funding will continue to be available 
in future years, or how schools will be determined eligible to apply.  Please review the RFP for 
information on the year it pertains to.   
 
13. I would like to inquire, if the SFA received this grant in FY 2020, would the RA be eligible to apply 
for it  again this year ? 
 
Answer:  No. SFAs that were awarded this grant in Fiscal Years 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023 are 
not eligible to apply for funding. A list of SFAs that previously received an equipment grant in 
these years is available here: Previous Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients . SFAs on this 
list are not eligible to apply for this grant opportunity  for any of their participating RAs.  
 
14. Are we eligible to apply for an equipment grant this year? I was told there is a list of schools that 
are not eligible if they received a grant within the last 3 years but I cannot find this list.  
 
Answer:  A list of SFAs that previously received an equipment grant in Fiscal Years 2020, 2021, 
2022, or 2023 is available here: Previous Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients . This link 
appears in the first page of the RFP . SFAs on this list are not eligible to apply for this grant 
opportunity.  
 
15. I’ve read through the RFP #97 and noticed SFAs that previously received awards in years 2020 -
2023 are not eligible. Do these include the RA’s as well?  
 

4 
 Answer:  Yes. For the purpose of this grant, eligible SFAs apply on behalf of their eligible RAs. 
If an SFA is included  on the list of SFAs that previously received an equipment grant in FY 2020, 
2021, 2022, or 2023, the SFA is not eligible to apply for any of their participating RAs. A list of 
SFAs that previously received an equipment grant in these years is available here: Previous 
Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients . 
 
16. If we are not in the N ational School Lunch Program (NSLP)  are we eligible?   We are in the Milk 
program.  
 
Answer:  No, eligible SFAs may apply for funding for their Recipient Agencies that participate 
in the NSLP . SFAs or RAs who do not participate in the NSLP are not eligible to apply.  
 
17. I'm not sure if we are eligible because  we had gotten an equipment grant a couple of  years ago. 
Our grant was RFP#GC23 -010 FY 2022. Does that make us ineligible to apply for RFP 97? For that 
grant, we had applied with our satellite  BEDS code . We also have  other satellite  BEDS codes, so 
I'm not sure if they might be eligible.   
 
Answer:  SFAs that were awarded this grant in Fiscal Years 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023 are not 
eligible to apply for funding. The list of previously awarded SFAs can be found here : Previous 
Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients . If any RA under an SFA received an award in the 
Fiscal Years 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023, the SFA is not eligible to apply for any of their RAs 
during this equipment grant.  
 
18. My district was approved to run an approved 4410 preschool program this past year and is in 
desperate need for new equipment for food.   While we received the grant as a school district, we 
did not have this program which is considered separate from the school district.   Can we apply for 
the preschool?  
 
Answer:  School Food Authorities (SFA) in New York State (NYS) that were not awarded this 
grant in Fiscal Years (FY) 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023 are eligible to apply for funding. A list of 
SFAs that previously received an equipment grant in FY 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2 023 is available 
here : Previous Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients . SFAs on this list are not eligible to 
apply for this grant opportunity  even if an individual  RA under the SFA has not received an 
award in one of the list years .  
 
19. I noticed my SFA is not eligible  for the equipment grant because they were awarded in FY 2023. I 
thought in previous  years it was by building and not by district. Are we able to apply for other 
buildings in the district?  
 
Answer:  For RFP 97 FY24 NSLP Equipment  Assistance  Grant , School Food Authorities (SFA) in 
New York State (NYS) that were not awarded this grant in Fiscal Years (FY) 2020, 2021, 2022, 
or 2023 are eligible to apply for funding. This eligibility requirement is different than previous 
grant years.  
 
If an SFA is listed on the Previous Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients  list, they are not 
eligible for this grant opportunity, and the application will not be considered for review or 
award.   
 

5 
 20. We are currently operating under C ommunity Eligibility Provision (CEP) .  In addition, we have fund 
balance.   Are we still eligible for this grant?  
 
Answer : Eligibility is not based on CEP status or fund balance.  
 
For RFP 97 FY24 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant, School Food Authorities (SFA) in New 
York State (NYS) that were not awarded this grant in Fiscal Years (FY) 2020, 2021, 2022, or 
2023 are eligible to apply for funding. Eligible SFAs may apply for funding fo r their Recipient 
Agencies (RA) that participate in the NSLP (including public schools, nonpublic schools, 
charter schools and residential childcare institutions).  This eligibility requirement is different 
than previous grant years.   
 
21. I am just seeking clarification on the language around this grant.   We did receive a grant in a 
previous year (2022) but we currently receive free lunches due to the community eligibility 
provision.   Would this preclude us from applying for this grant?  
 
Answer:  Yes. Eligibility is not based on CEP status. School Food Authorities (SFA) in New York 
State that were not awarded an equipment grant in Fiscal Years (FY) 2020, 2021, 2022, or 
2023 are eligible to apply for funding.  Eligible SFAs may apply for funding for their Recipient 
Agencies (RA) that participate in the NSLP (including public schools, nonpublic schools, 
charter schools and residential childcare institutions).  
 
If an SFA is listed on the Previous Food Service Equipment Grant Recipients list, they are not 
eligible for this grant opportunity, and the application will not be considered for review or 
award.   
 
 
Equipment  
 
22. Would the replacement of a freezer door be an acceptable use of funds?  
 
Answer:  Yes, replacement of a freezer door could be an acceptable use of funds. Equipment 
requests may include new equipment, used equipment, and replacement of equipment with 
a per item acquisition cost greater than $1,000.  
 
23. If we were awarded the equipment grant funds, could those grant funds be used for a prior 
purchase? For example, if we installed a walk -in freezer over the summer (after July 1), can the 
grant money be applied to equipment previously purchased?  
 
Answer:  This grant does not apply to equipment that has already been purchased . 
Please see the “Project Period” and “Equipment Requests” sections of the RFP.  
 
24. We need a new walk -in freezer. Can we use grant funds towards equipment to reduce cost or does 
the grant have to cover the total cost of the equipment?  
 
Answer:  Yes, SFAs may be awarded up to a maximum of $20,000 in equipment for each 
eligible RA. In the case an equipment item is needed that exceeds the $20,000 limit, the SFA 

6 
 may apply for up to $20,000 to be put toward the purchase of this item, so long as the SFA is 
willing to cover the difference in cost from their own funds.  
 
25. Can you put in for something like a walk -in freezer? I know the grant would not cover the total 
cost of the freezer but is it possible to get a partial amount to put towards a new freezer?  
 
Answer:  Yes, SFAs may be awarded up to a maximum of $20,000 in equipment for each eligible 
RA. In the case an equipment item is needed that exceeds the $20,000 limit, the SFA may apply 
for up to $20,000 to be put toward the purchase of this item, so long as the SFA is willing to 
cover the difference in cost from their own funds.  
 
26. When looking at bids, if an estimate is over the $20,000 threshold and we have secured funding 
beyond that, can we still apply, or does the amount and application have to be under $20,000 ?  
 
Question:  Yes, SFAs may be awarded up to a maximum of $20,000 in equipment for each 
eligible RA. In the case an equipment item exceeds the $20,000 limit, the SFA may apply for 
up to $20,000 to be put toward the purchase of this item, so long as the SFA is willing to 
cover the difference in cost.  
 
27. If an SFA wants to purchase a new P oint of Sale (POS)  terminal with this grant, would new POS 
software be an acceptable use of additional grants funds? The software my district is looking at 
combines a front of house POS system with back of house nutrition system which would allow us 
to better plan nutrition  and drive more participation.  
 
Answer:  Yes, both the school food service POS terminal/computer and school food service 
POS software are allowable requests . The individual equipment requests must have a value 
greater than $1,000 as described in the “Equipment Requests” section of the RFP .  If the SFA 
will consider the entire POS system (all components together instead of individual pieces) to 
be equipment fo r financial statement purposes rather than supplies and materials, the SFA 
should submit a written statement on letterhead indicating  this. If the SFA does not indicate 
in writing with the application that the individual components of the POS system will be 
combined and considered equipment, the cost of the individual POS components will be 
evaluated by NYSED to determine if each item h as a value greater than $1,000, as required . 
 
Please review the “Application Form” and “Equipment Request s” section of the RFP .  
 
28.  What constitutes General Equipment? For instance, we're looking to get temp probes for all of 
our refrigerated spaces to ensure proper temperature monitoring. It's a tangible piece of 
equipment, but not like an oven or stove in size. Also, is there a way t o order for the district since 
it's all coming from one source? IE we have a quote for the entire district as a bundle instead of 
school by school for the bulk discount.  
 
Answer:  Regulations at 2 CFR Part 200.1 define equipment as tangible personal property, 
having a useful life of more than one year and a per -unit acquisition cost that equals or 
exceeds the lesser of the capitalization level established by the non -Federal entity f or financial 
statement purposes, or $10,000 per unit. However, for the FY 2024 NSLP Equipment 
Assistance Grant, Congress has specified that the threshold for the purchase of equipment 
has been lowered to $1,000.  Multiple items whose per -unit acquis ition cost is less than 

7 
 $1,000 may not be combined to meet the minimum value of greater than $1,000. Under no 
circumstance will a grant be awarded for an item that does not have an acquisition cost 
greater than $1,000.  
 
SFAs may apply for  food service equipment, with a value of greater than $1,000, needed to 
serve healthier meals; support scratch cooking; improve the overall quality of meals; improve 
food safety; and expand access and help to support the establishment, maintenance, or 
expansion of the S chool Breakfast Program (SBP).  
  
Awarded SFAs must follow proper procurement when procuring awarded items.  Review the 
“Equipment Requests” and “Procurement” sections of the RFP .

Purpose of 
Grant  The School Food Service Equipment Grant is intended to improve the infrastructure of the 
National School Lunch Program (NSLP) . This will be achieved by providing the opportunity for 
schools to purchase equipment to serve healthier meals, improve the overall quality of meals, 
improve food safety , expand participation in  school meals programs , and help to support  the 
establishment, maintenance, or expansion of the School Breakfast Program.  
 
 
 
 
Eligible 
Applicants  School Food Authorit ies (SFA)  in New York State  (NYS)  that were not awarded this grant in Fiscal 
Years (FY) 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023 are eligible to apply for funding.   Eligible SFAs may apply 
for funding for their R ecipient Agencies (R A) that participate in the NSLP  (including public 
school s, nonpublic schools, charter schools and residential childcare institutions).  
 The SFA will apply on behalf of their eligible RAs.  Unless otherwise exempt, as detailed in this 
RFP,  the SFA will submit a separate application for each piece of requested equipment for an 
eligible RA.

Guidance Manual  
Introduction  
 
The Fiscal Year ( FY) 202 4, Consolidated Appropriations Act  (Public Law 11 8-42), has provided funding in the 
amount of  $10,000,000 to be distributed to State Agencies (SA s) that will competitively award equipment 
assistance grants  to eligible  School  Food  Authorities  (SFA s) participating  in the National  School  Lunch  Program  
(NSLP) . 
 
These funds will allow SFAs to purchase equipment , with a value of greater than $1,000, needed to serve 
healthier meals ; support scratch cooking; improve the overall quality of meals ; improve  food  safety; and 
expand access  and help to support the establishment, maintenance, or expansion of the School Breakfast 
Program  (SBP) .  
 The equipment purchased with the FY  2024 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant must be used to support the 
federally assisted school meals programs. Equipment may not be purchased exclusively for programs outside 
of the federally assisted school meals programs.  When a Recipient Agency (R A) participates in other school 
meal programs [such as the School Breakfast Program (SBP), Afterschool Snack Program (ASP), Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program (FFVP), Summer Food Service Program (SFSP)], in addition to the NSLP, those other meals programs may benefit from  equipment purchased with FY  2024 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant funds. For 
example, if an RA participating in the NSLP and SBP purchases a new refrigerator with the FY 202 4 NSLP  
Equipment  Assistance Grant  funds,  food  items  for both federal programs  may  be stored  in the refrigerator.  
 The SFA will apply on behalf of their eligible Recipient Agencies ( RAs). Unless otherwise exempt, as detailed 
in this Request for P roposals (RFP),  the SFA will submit a separate application for each piece of requested 
equipment for an eligible RA.   
 
This project has been funded at least in part with f ederal funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The 
contents of this publication do not necessarily reflect the view or policies of the U.S. Department of Agriculture,  
nor does  mention  of trade  names,  commercial  products,  or organizations  imply  endorsement by the U.S.  
Government.  
 
Project Period  
 
The project period for this grant is 7/1/ 2025 - 6/30/2026. SFAs must obligate their full grant award by 
September 30, 2025.  All procurement and expenditure activities must be completed no later than 
6/30/2026.  
 
Eligible Applicants  
 
All SFAs that did not receive a previous grant award through the FY2020, 2021, 2022 or 2023 National School Lunch Program Equipment Assistance Grant for School Food Authorities are eligible to apply for funding for their RAs that participate in the NSLP, i ncluding public schools, nonpublic schools, charter schools and 


   
 
 6 residential childcare institutions in New York State.  
 
Applicants should review the RFP in its entirety to ensure the application is completed accurately.  
 
New SFAs and new RAs  in their first year of operation must receive formal approval  by the New York State 
Education Department (NYSED)  Child  Nutrition  Program  Office  to participate  in the NSLP  by the submission 
deadline  of June 1 6, 202 5, at 5:00 p.m.  for the FY 2024 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant Application to  be 
eligible to apply for funding.   
 
Selected SFAs/RAs must operate the NSLP and be in good standing with all Child Nutrition Programs.   
 
Failure to abide by the requirements and regulations of all Child Nutrition Programs and/or termination from 
any federal or state Child Nutrition Program prior to award and/or throughout the grant award period may result in ineligibility and/or immediate loss of the awarded grant and disallowance of Equipment Grant reimbursements and recoupment of equipment grant funding. Termination from the NSLP prior to award and/or throughout the grant award period will result in immediate loss of the awarded grant and disallowance 
of Equipment Grant reimbursements.  
 
Prequalification Requirement - Required for Non -Public SFAs and Charter School  SFAs

Management  website) designed to facilitate prompt contracting for not -for-profit vendors. All not -for-profit 
vendors are required to prequalify by the grant application deadline to receive an award under this  RFP.  This 
includes  all currently  funded not-for-profit  institutions  that have  already  received  an award and are in the 
middle of the program cycle. Please review the additional information regarding this requirement below . 
 
Please be advised, this requirement applies to all non- public SFAs and to all charter school  SFAs.

Workers’ Compensation Coverage and Debarment  
 
New York State Workers’ Compensation Law (WCL) has specific coverage requirements for businesses 
contracting with New York State and additional requirements that provide for the debarment of vendors that violate certain sections of WCL. The WCL requires, a nd has required since introduction of the law in 1922, the 
heads of all municipal and State entities to ensure that businesses have appropriate workers’ compensation and disability benefits insurance coverage prior  to issuing any permits or licenses, or pr ior to entering into 
contracts.  
 Workers’ compensation requirements are covered by WCL Section 57, while disability benefits are covered by 
WCL Section 220(8). The Workers’ Compensation Benefits clause in Appendix A – STANDARD CLAUSES FOR 
NEW YORK STATE CONTRACTS states that in accordance with Sec tion 142 of the State Finance Law, a contract 
shall be void and of no force and effect unless the contractor provides and maintains coverage during the life of the contract for the benefit of such employees as are required to be covered by the provisions o f the WCL.  
 Under provisions of the 2007 Workers’ Compensation Reform Legislation (WCL Section 141 -b), any person, or 
entity substantially owned by that person: subject to a final assessment of civil fines or penalties, subject to a stop- work order, or convicted of a misdemeanor for violation of Workers’ Compensation laws Section 52 or 
131, is barred from bidding on, or being awarded, any public work contract or subcontract with the State, any 
municipal corporation or public body for one year for each violation. The ban is five years for each felony 

   
 
 8 conviction.

Focus of SFA Grants  
 
The equipment request and grant application submission must address how the equipment improves the 
quality of school meals.  
 
The application will also address one  focus area from the following: 
 
• Focus 1: Food Safety  
 
Equipment that improves the safety of food served in the school nutrition programs (e.g., cold/hot holding equipment, dishwashing equipment, refrigeration, milk coolers, freezers, blast chillers, etc.)  
 
• Focus 2: Serving Healthier School  Meals  
 
Equipment that allows for preparing, cooking , and serving healthier school meals, scratch cooking  and 
increasing nutritional quality (e.g., salad bars,  storage of fresh food,  steaming equipment, refrigeration units).  
 
• Focus 3: Expanded Participation  in NSLP and/or SBP  
 
Equipment that allows SFAs to support expanded participation in the NSLP  and/or SBP (e.g., equipment for 
serving meals in a non- traditional setting or to better utilize cafeteria space  or equipment that will help to 
support the establishment, maintenance, or expansion of the SBP .) 
 
Equipment Requests  
 Regulations at 2 CFR Part 200 .1 define equipment as tangible personal property, having a useful life of more 
than one year and a per -unit acquisition cost that equals or exceeds the lesser of the capitalization level 
established by the non -Federal entity for financial statement purposes, or $ 10,000 per unit. However, for the 
FY 2024 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant, Congress has specified that the threshold for the purchase of 
equipment has been lowered to $1,000.  This definition will be used for purposes of this grant and recording 
of equipment costs.  
 
Equipment requests may include new equipment, used equipment, and replacement of equipment with a per 
item acquisition cost greater than $1,000 . This grant does not apply to equipment that has already been 
purchased. SFAs may receive up to $20,000 in equipment for each eligible RA.  
 
Multiple items whose per -unit acquisition cost is less than $1,000 may not be combined to meet the minimum 
value of greater than $1,000.  Under no circumstance will a grant be awarded for an item that does not have an acquisition cost greater than $1,000.  
  Grant funding may not be used to purchase items that are used solely for the sale of a la carte products.  
 As with all federal funds, the equipment purchases must be necessary, reasonable, and allocable. Using these funds to purchase a walk -in freezer for school nutrition programs is an allowable cost; however, renovation of 
the school nutrition area would fall under the category of construction costs, which must be charged to the 
school general fund or capital outlay fund . 
 
New York State must comply with the statutory requirement that grants are to be based on the need for 
equipment assistance in participating RAs.  
 
SFAs should consider and address the following factors, as applicable, when answering the grant application 

   
 
 10 questions:  
• How the equipment will benefit the  school meals programs including contribution to improving 
quality of school  meals  
• The availability of existing State and Local funding for equipment purchases  
• Age of current food service  equipment or lack of appropriate items  
• Strategies for adopting cafeteria changes that provide more convenience and appeal to the student  
• Opportunities to realize a meaningful impact on nutrition and quality of  school meals  
 
Acquisition Cost  
 
Acquisition  cost is defined  as the net invoice  unit price  of the property,  including the cost of modifications, 
attachments, accessories, or auxiliary apparatus necessary to make the property usable for the purpose for  
which  it was acquired.  Other  charges  such  as the cost of installation,  transportation,  duty  or protective in -transit 
insurance, shall be included or excluded from the unit acquisition cost in accordance with the grantee’s regular 
accounting practices. The cost of building renovation or construction of school nutrition areas are not included 
under acquisition costs.

Method of Awarding Grants  
 
Application Scoring  
 Each application will be  separately  reviewed  and scored by two reviewers. The scores of the two reviewers will 
be averaged to obtain the final average score.  
 
A third  review  will be performed  if there  is a difference  of eight  (8) points  or more  between  the two scores. In 
cases where a third review is necessary, all three scores will be averaged to obtain the final average score.  
 
Applications will be ranked according to score from highest to lowest. In a case where two or more applicants receive the same evaluation score and funds are not available to fully fund those applications, the application that received the highest average score on question 2a under Section 2 of the Selection Criteria Form will be ranked higher. If there is also a tie score on question 2a, the average score for question 1a in Section 1 will be used as the tie- breaker. The Recipient Agency’s enrollment from  the most recent claim for reimbursement at 
the time awards are made will be used as a third tie -breaker, if necessary. Using the third tie -breaker, RAs with 
the highest enrollment will be awarded first.  
 
Awards will be made for applications in rank order of average final score until funds are exhausted or there 
are no fundable applications remaining.  
 If any remaining  funds  are insufficient  to award  the next -highest  ranked  eligible  application  in full, that applicant 
will be offered a partial award.   No SFA may receive more than a combined $20,000 for an individual Recipient  Agency.  
 
NYSED will not consider any unallowable or inappropriate items from the SFA’s/RA’s requests.  
 
Award s will be made to SFAs for their eligible RAs for specific equipmen t pieces for specific dollar amounts.

grants.title: 2024 Title I School Improvement Grant 1003 (Planning)
grants.summary: Funds planning and development of district and school improvement plans under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA).
grants.description: The 2024 Title I School Improvement Grant 1003 (Planning) provides funding to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) for Target Districts and schools identified for Comprehensive Support and Improvement (CSI), Additional Targeted Support and Improvement (ATSI), and Targeted Support and Improvement (TSI). The funds support the development and implementation of continuous improvement plans for the 2024–25 school year. Eligible activities include needs assessments, parent/family participation, survey administration, and planning support. Applications must be submitted online through the NYSED Business Portal and certified by the chief school officer.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible districts include newly identified Target Districts and schools previously identified for LSI with at least one subgroup in the TSI support model. Charter schools and districts with schools identified for LSI, ATSI, or CSI are not eligible.
key_requirements: LEAs must complete all sections of the online application.
Applications must be certified by the chief school officer.
FS-10 budget form must align proposed expenses to planning activities.
Funds must be encumbered during the project period (February 1, 2024 to August 31, 2024).
No carryover of funds is allowed.

 Full RFP – Application Information 
The online application is available to LEAs through the NYSED Business Portal . Select the survey 
titled “2024 Title I School Improvement Grant 1003 (Planning).” 
Purpose of 2024 Title I School Improvement Grant (SIG) 1003 (Planning) Funds 
Section 1003 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) requires that State Education Agencies allocate funds to LEAs for Target Districts and schools identified for Comprehensive Support and Improvement (CSI), Additional Targeted Support and Improvement 
(ATSI), and Targeted Support and Improvement (TSI) to support the development and 
implementation of their individual district and school continuous improvement plans.  The 2024 
SIG Planning funds are provided to support the planning and development of the 2024 –25 district 
and school improvement plans as required under the ESEA . 
Eligibility District -Level Improvement Plan Development 
The following districts are eligible for 2024 Title I SIG Planning funding to support the development of the district- level improvement plan : 
• Newly Identified Target Districts 
The following districts are not eligible for 2024 Title I SIG Planning funding to support the 
development of the district- level improvement plan: 
• Previously Identified Target Districts* 
School -Level Improvement Plan Development 
Districts with the following schools are eligible for 2024 Title I SIG Planning funding to support 
the development of school -level plans: 
• Schools Previously Identified for LSI that now have at least one subgroup in the 
TSI support model 
Districts with the following schools are not eligible for 2024 Title I SIG Planning funding to 
support the development of school -level plans: 
• Districts that only have schools identified for L SI 
• Schools identified for LSI, ATSI *, or CSI* 
• Schools newly identified for TSI that were identified for CSI or ATSI last year* 
• Schools re -identified for TSI* 
• Charter schools 
*Re-Identified Target Districts , and Schools that began the 2023–24 SY in the TSI, ATSI 
or CSI support model and remain identified should access the 2023- 24 Title I SIG Basic funding 
to support the development of their 2024–25 improvement plans. 
See Attachment I for a list of Target Dist ricts and Title I SIG Planning funding allocations .  The 
individual support model for districts and schools can be found online at: 
https://data.nysed.gov/ . 

 
      
    
    
    
  
 
  
    
  
   
  
   
  
 
 
  
 
 
 
  
   
     
     
 
     
 
 
 
   
    
   
  
  
       
  
 
  
      
 
            
            
               
           Funding 
Eligible districts and schools will receive the following allocations for 2024 Title I SIG Planning: 
• Newly Identified Target District -$20,000 per district 
• Schools previously identified for LSI that now have at least one subgroup identified for T SI -$20,000 per school 
Allowable Activities Districts may use 2024 Title I SIG Planning funds for the following activities: 
CATEGORY 1: Staff participation in the completion of needs assessment activities and the 
development of the 2024 -25 district -level and/or school -level improvement plan(s) 
CATEGORY 2: Support for parent/family participation in the development of the 20 24-25 
district -level and/or school -level improvement plan(s ) 
CATEGORY 3: Administration and/or analysis of family, staff, and student surveys as part 
of the needs assessment process 
CATEGORY 4: BOCES Needs Assessment and Planning Support* * 
**If your BOCES does not provide Needs Assessment and Planning Support and you would like to use SIG Planning 
Funds for external support, please contact fieldsupport@nysed.gov. 
Submission Instructions: 
• LEAs must complete all sections of the online application and are required to answer questions marked with a red asterisk. If a required question has not been completed, 
the business portal will highlight it in red and the section of the application will be flagged. The applicant will be unable to submit the application to NYSED for final r eview 
if a required question remains unresolved. 
• The online application may only be submitted/certified by the chief school officer of the applicant LEA. The designated superintendent of an LEA is the only administrator with the submit/certify rights necessary to successfully submit and certify a completed application for NYSED review. 
• The FS -10 budget ( Excel version preferred ) should be completed in a manner that clearly 
identifies and aligns proposed expenses to planning activities. In addition, be sure to 
specify if activities are occurring at the district or school building level. Please see the annotated sample FS- 10 in the Documents panel. 
Completed applications are due by April 14, 2024 and will be reviewed on a rolling basis. LEAs 
are encouraged to submit as soon as possible to expedite the review and approval process of 2024 SIG Planning funds. 
LEAs are REQUIRED to send a blue ink signed original and two hard copies of an FS -10 budget 
form to: 
NYS Education Department -Office of Accountability 
Attn: 2024 Title I SIG 1003 (Planning) 
89 Washington Avenue -Room 320 EB 
Albany, NY 12234 

 
  
 
       
  
 
 
  
  
 
    
 
 
 
 
  Project Period 
February 1, 2024 to August 31, 2024. 
Completed applications are due by April 14, 2024 and will be reviewed on a rolling basis. LEAs 
are encouraged to submit as soon as possible to expedite the review and approval process of 
2024 SIG Planning funds. 
There is no carryover for these funds. All costs must be encumbered during the project period. 
Budget Amendment Deadline 
All budget amendments should be discussed with the program office prior to the submission of 
an FS- 10A. Amendments must be submitted with sufficient time for review and be postmarked 
no later than August 1, 2024. 
Questions 
For additional information or assistance, please contact: SIGA@nysed.gov

grants.title: 2023-2024 Statewide Universal Full-Day Prekindergarten (SUFDPK) Expansion Grant
grants.summary: This grant funds the creation of new full-day prekindergarten placements or the conversion of half-day placements to full-day placements for four-year-old students in New York State.
grants.description: The 2023-2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant aims to increase the availability of high-quality prekindergarten programming for four-year-old students in New York State. Eligible applicants are public school districts, which can use the funds to create new full-day placements or convert existing half-day placements to full-day. Programming must align with New York State Learning Standards and address student and community needs. Applications must be submitted by January 24, 2024, and must include one original and two paper copies. Interested districts should refer to the RFP for detailed eligibility and submission requirements.
grants.award_text: $10,000 or $7,000 per pupil for new or converted seats
grants.eligibility_notes: All public school districts in New York State are eligible to apply. Community-based organizations (CBOs) cannot apply directly but may collaborate with school districts.
key_requirements: Applicants must be public school districts in New York State.
Funds must be used to create new full-day placements or convert half-day placements to full-day for four-year-old students.
Programming must align with New York State Learning Standards and Education Law §3602-ee.
Applications must include one original and two paper copies.
Submission deadline is January 24, 2024, by 5:00 PM.

Questions and Answers for GC 23 -021 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion Grant for 
New Full- Day and Half -Day to Full -Day Placements for Four -Year -Old Students  
1 
  
Update: The application due date has been extended. Receipt of 
1 original and 2 paper copies must be received by 5:00 PM, 
January 24, 2024.  
 
   
Eligibility  
 Q1: We are interested in the 2024 - 2025 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion 
Grant.  Is this opportunity available? If so, what are the guidelines and next 
steps to apply?   
 A: The 2023- 2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant is for the 2023- 2024 school year. If 
awarded , funds would be available in the 2024- 2025 school  year. The RFP 
and 
other documents are posted to the Funding Opportunities  website.  
 Q2: Please clarify if this RFP is for  Districts or  if CBO'S can apply, as  well.  
In addition is there a way that we could  change our current contract to another 
entity with a different EIN number.  
 A: All public -school  districts are eligible to apply for this funding opportunity. Potential 
agency and CBO prekindergarten collaborators are not eligible to directly apply for this funding opportunity. However, these eligible organizations are encouraged to apply to a school  district to be considered for collaborative prekindergarten 
programming.  Please see page 5 of the RFP
 for Eligibility requirements.  
 Q3: Can districts who have already applied (but were denied) reapply?  
 A: Yes. This is a new grant award opportunity, and all eligible districts are encouraged 
to apply. Please refer to page 5 of the RFP
 for the eligibility requirements.  
 Q4: Some New York State school districts have a December  31 cut -off for 
kindergarten which presumes that their Pre- K cut off would also be Dec ember  
31. How would the  Expansion Grant’s Dec ember  1 eligibility cut -off for Pre -K 
affect these Districts ? Would Districts be eligible to apply for and receive 
funding for students turning four  between December  1 and 31?  
 A:  Yes, districts are eligible to apply for this RFP whether using December 1 or 31
st for 
prekindergarten eligibility age cut -off. School districts notify NYSED of their chosen 
prekindergarten eligibility age cut -off dates annually via their State- Administered 
Prekindergarten Application. Such dates are then reported to the Office of 
Information and Reporting Services, so students are counted correctly in SIRS . 


Questions and Answers for GC 23 -021 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion Grant for 
New Full- Day and Half -Day to Full -Day Placements for Four -Year -Old Students  
2 
 These dates are then applied to grades PreK -  12. All UPK and SUFDPK  expansion 
grant funding sources use the same reported age cut -off dates.  
 
Q5: Is the email below referencing the same SUFDPK  expanded grant that the 
district  was already awarded?  
 A: No. This is a new funding opportunity. All public -school  districts are eligible to apply.  
Please refer to page 5 of the RFP
 for the eligibility requirements.  
   Q6: In reading the RFP it appears that my district  is not considered "SUFDPK ”.  
Can we apply and is it expected to add new Prekindergarten classrooms?  
 A: Yes, this funding opportunity is open to all public -school  districts. The purpose of the 
2023- 2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant for four -year-old students is to increase the 
availability of high -quality prekindergarten placements for high needs students and 
schools within New York State. Grant funds must be used to create new full -day 
placements or to convert existing half -day prekindergarten placements to full -day, for 
four-year old students. Please refer to the RFP
 for eligibility and submission 
requirements.  
Q7: Do new full day slots have to be for additional students, beyond what the 
district is currently serving —even if the district is already serving more than 
its minimum required number? For example,  if a district is serving 60 
students and only gets funding f or 40, could the other 20 students be 
considered new full day slots?  
 A: Yes. The purpose of the 2023- 2024 SUFDPK  Expansion Grant for four -year-old 
students is to increase the availability of high- quality prekindergarten placements for 
high needs students and schools within New York State. Grant funds must be used to create new full -day placements or to convert exist ing half -day prekindergarten 
placements to full -day, for four -year old students.  
 
Q8: Alternatively, we think that we will need to expand from two to three  
classrooms. Would this make us eligible for the grant?  
 A: This funding opportunity is open to all public -school  districts . The purpose of the 
2023- 2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant  for four -year-old students is to increase the 
availability of high -quality prekindergarten placements for high needs students and 
schools wi thin New York State. Grant funds must be used to create new full -day 
placements or to convert existing half -day prekindergarten placements to full -day, for 
four-year old students.  Programming must be aligned with applicable New York 
State Learning Standards along with relevant Education Law §3602- ee requirements 
and address student and community need.  Please refer to the RFP
 for eligibility and 
submission requirements.  
 

Questions and Answers for GC 23 -021 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion Grant for 
New Full- Day and Half -Day to Full -Day Placements for Four -Year -Old Students  
3 
 Q9: If we started a UPK program this year with two classrooms (using the state 
and federal funds available to all Districts across the state), can we still apply 
for the "2023- 2024 Statewide Universal Full -Day Prekindergarten (SUFDPK) 
Expansion Grant" ?  
 
A: Yes, this is a new funding opportunity open to all public -school  districts  regardless of 
other funding sources . If awarded, grant funds must be used to create new full -day 
placements or to convert existing half -day prekindergarten placements to full -day, for 
four-year old students. Programming must be aligned with applicable New  York 
State Learning Standards along with relevant Education Law §3602- ee requirements 
and address student and community need.  
 
Q10: What data is reflected in the determination of the economically 
disadvantaged percentage rates for which bonus points are awarded?   
 
A: As defined by data.nysed.gov, economically disadvantaged  students are those who 
participate in or whose family participates in economic assistance programs . Using 
publicly available  data, a frequency analysis was  conducted to compare each 
districts ’ percentage of economically disadvantaged students against t he state 
average (54%) . Using 54% as the baseline, frequency bands were identified. See 
Appendix F  for district specific data.   
 
Funding  
 
Q11:  If a District is awarded funds from this grant and it has an established 
collaborative partnership, is the $10,000 or $7,000 per pupil rate only be applicable to additional students and not to those who have previously enrolled in the CBO at the lower funding rate of around $ 5400? For example, 
would the CBO now receive two different tuition reimbursements for the remainder of the school year, one for previously enrolled students and one for newly enrolled with Expansion Grant funds if the district  did a 90-day 
program to serve children on their waiting list for the remainder of the school year? The following year, if the district  continues to have the 
Expansion Grant, would the CBO then receive the higher tuition rate for all students? 
 A: Yes, the $10,000 a nd $7,000 per pupil rate would be specifically for new seats or 
half-day to full day  converted seats. Funding is based on student enrollment; 
therefore, a CBO could receive two different per pupil reimbursements depending on number of students enrolled how  they are funded. Partnerships and funding 
determinations are a district decision.  
 Q12: For current CBO programs that transitioned from half day to full day using 
our original  funding allocations for the 2023 -2024 school year, will they be 
funded at the current rate or the new $10,000 or $7,000 rate if we were to 

Questions and Answers for GC 23 -021 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion Grant for 
New Full- Day and Half -Day to Full -Day Placements for Four -Year -Old Students  
4 
 apply and be granted this opportunity? If any current full day seats will be 
funded at the original rate, how are districts to address this inequity?  
 A:  If awarded,  the district would only receive the proper amount based upon the 
qualifications of the teacher. If the students are placed in a new full -day placement 
with a certified teacher, the district would receive $10,000 per student. If the students are placed in a new full -day slot with an uncertified teacher, the district 
would receive $7,000 per student. The total amount the district can receive each 
year cannot exceed their initial grant award amount.  CBOs are funded based on the 
partnership agreements between the district and CBO.  
 Q13: Can a district or BOCES use this funding to cover the expansion of pre -K 
programming in classrooms that have a mix of three - and four -year-old students?  
 A: No. This funding opportunity is only applicable to four -year-old students. If a district 
has a multi -aged prekindergarten classroom, the fund from this award can only be 
utilized for the four -year-old students.  
 
Q14: We have received information from OEL that our District is eligible for 20 
full-time PreK Students and 56 Half -day PreK Students. Our program 
Director contacted OEL and was assured that this funding was also 
available for the 24 -25 school year as we are in 24- 25 budget development 
currently. We currently only operate a half -day UPK program. Do we have to 
apply to the RFP referenced in order to secure our maximum funding for 24 -
25?  
 A: The 2023- 2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant is a new funding source for the purpose 
of establishing new full -day seats or for converting current half -day seats to full -day 
on top of what is already served. According to Education Law 3602- e (10)
, “Subject 
to an available appropriation in the State budget for this purpose and provided all requirements of this grant and §3602- ee quality standards have been met, all 
awarded school districts will retain their 180- day maximum grant award in the 2024-
2025 school year and thereafter.” The total amount the district can receive each year cannot exceed their initial grant award amount. Partnerships and funding determinations are a district decision.  
Q15: We have a grant this year for about $90,000 added to our base 
allocation.  Since we qualified last year for it and are starting to use it this 
year, do we have to apply every year or is it something that we will get until no additional funding is available ?  
A: No, as a 2022- 2023 awardee you do not have to reapply for this funding annually.  
According to Education Law 3602- e (10)
 prior grant awards are s ubject to an 
available appropriation in the State budget for this purpose and provided all 
requirements of this grant and §3602- ee quality standards have been met, all 
awarded school districts will retain their 180- day maximum grant award in the 2024-
2025 school year and thereaf ter. 

Questions and Answers for GC 23 -021 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion Grant for 
New Full- Day and Half -Day to Full -Day Placements for Four -Year -Old Students  
5 
 Q16: Once awarded, does a district have to reapply for the expansion grant each 
year? Since the SUFDPK  Grant was awarded for 202 2-2023, does the district 
have to reapply for this current grant (2023 -2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant), 
or is the grant money provided annually to the district after the initial 
grant  award?  
A: No, awardees do not have to reapply for this funding annually . According to 
Education Law 3602- e (10)  prior grant awards are subject to an available 
appropriation in the State budget for this purpose and provided all  requirements of 
this grant and §3602- ee quality standards have been met, all awarded school 
districts will retain their 180 -day maximum grant award in the 2024- 2025 school year 
and thereafter.  
Q17: As per the RFP i t looks  as though a district would receive $10,000 per 
student if the student is served by a teacher of record with New York State teacher certification valid for service in the early childhood grades or students with disabilities . If a district were converting t o half day to full day 
seats, would the district receive another $10,000 per student totaling it to $20,000 per student?  
A: No. The district will receive either $10,000 per student for a certified teacher or 
$7,000 a student per uncertified teacher for new  full-day seats. If converting from 
half-day to full -day seats, the district receives a portion depending upon their 
conversion rate. For district specific conversion rates, please see Appendix B
. 
Q18: If a District receives the Expansion Grant, in the future, will the funding 
allotment now become $10,000 or $7,000 (depending on teacher certification) per all pre -K students receiving pre -k funding from New York State as long 
as the district  has the Expan sion Grant? 
 A: No. If awarded this grant, other allocations and grant amounts are not impacted. 
Districts who receive this grant award will be awarded $10,000 per student with a certified teacher of record with New York State teacher certification valid f or service in 
the early childhood grades or a teaching license or certificate for students with disabilities valid for service in early childhood grades or $7,000 per student with an uncertified teacher of record.  
 Q19: We added a third UPK section of 18 students in 2023- 2024.  The cost for 
three sections of UPK is $443,140.  Our current Federal/NYS allocation  totals 
$318,384 leaving a local share of $124,756.  Can the SUFDPK Expansion 
Grant be used to cover the local share?  
 A: No. The purpose of  2023- 2024 SUFDPK Expansion Grant is for  establishing new 
full-day seats or for converting current half -day seats to full -day on top of what is 
already served.  
 

Questions and Answers for GC 23 -021 Universal Prekindergarten Expansion Grant for 
New Full- Day and Half -Day to Full -Day Placements for Four -Year -Old Students  
6 
 Q20: We currently have a ½  day program with groups coming to us in the AM & 
PM. Would any funding that we received be a one -time disbursement, or 
would it be spread throughout several years? We have discussed moving to

availabi lity of high -quality prekindergarten placements for high needs students and schools within New 
York State. This competitive grant initiative builds on the foundation established by the $1.2 billion 
investment in prekindergarten across the state.  
Grant funds must be used to create new full -day placements or to convert existing half -day 
prekindergarten placements to full -day, for four -year old students .  
 
Eligible Applicants:  
All public  school districts are eligible to apply. Preference for the 2023- 2024 awards will be awarded 
as bonus points  to districts serving high level of economically disadvantaged  studen ts. Economically -
disadvantaged students are those who participate in, or whose f amily participates in, economic 
assistance programs, such as the free or reduced- price lunch programs, Social Security Insurance 
(SSI), Food Stamps, Foster Care, Refugee Assistance (cash or medical assistance), Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC), Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP), Safety Net Assistance (SNA), Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), or Family Assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF). If one student in a family is identified as low income, all students from that household (economic  unit) 
may be identified as low income (
data.nysed.gov  Glossary of Terms).

opportunity. CBOs are encouraged to apply to a school district to be considered for contracting collaborative prekindergarten programming.  Potential collaborating eligible agencies / CBOs include 
providers of approved, licensed and/or registered prekindergarten programs, such as those associated with:

 Days of Operation  
Awards under this grant program will be based on the NYSED -approved number of New Full-Day and 
Half-Day to Full -Day prekindergarten placements for four -year-old students served by NYS -certified 
and uncertified prekindergarten teachers in a 180- day school year.

for a minimum of 90 days. Otherwise, awarded school districts will be able to operate a 180- day 
program during the 2024- 2025 school year.

serve, and which students will be placed on a waiting list .

 Method of Award:  
Each eligible proposal will be reviewed by at least two reviewers. Each reviewer will score the proposal according to the indica ted point criteria in the Proposal Narrative and the Budget Narrative using the 
Proposal Evaluation Rubric in Appendix  D. Bonus p oints based on economically disadvantaged 
percentage data will be auto matically  generated. Scores from each reviewer will be averaged to 
compute the final score. If there is a difference of more than 15 points between the two reviewers’ scores, a third reviewer will review the application and the two closest scores will be averaged to compute the final score. In those instances where the third review falls equally between the initial two scores, the score of the third review will be used as the final score. A third review will not be required when it is mathematically impossible for an applicant to achieve an average score of 60 or higher with 
a third review.  
 Budgets will be adjusted to eliminate any unallowable or inappropriate expenditure.  
  
Proposals that receive a final average score of 60 or more, excluding bonus points,  will be considered 
for funding.  
 Awards will be made starting with the highest scoring proposal in rank order for all other districts.  
 In the event of tie scores, proposals with the highest combined score on Section 2 Need Narrative will be ranked higher. If a tie remains,  the proposal with the highest combined score on Section 4 Program 
Quality Narrative will be ranked higher.

[§3602- e (17)] and [8 NYCRR 151- 1.3 (b)(2)]

interim progress monitoring that takes place two to three times per year. More frequent progress 
monitoring (formal or informal) may occur throughout the year as needed.  
 
A child’s developmental baseline is typically established by the first administration of the interim 
progress monitoring tool. This provides a comprehensive evaluation of the level of skills, abilities

grants.title: FY 2023 National School Lunch Program Equipment Assistance Grant for School Food Authorities
grants.summary: This grant funds the purchase of equipment to improve the infrastructure of the National School Lunch Program (NSLP).
grants.description: The grant aims to enhance the infrastructure of the National School Lunch Program by providing funding for schools to purchase equipment. This equipment will help serve healthier meals, improve meal quality, ensure food safety, expand participation in school meal programs, and support the establishment or expansion of the School Breakfast Program. Eligible applicants must follow the detailed instructions in the RFP, including prequalification requirements for non-public and charter schools. Applications must be submitted via the SharePoint site by the deadline.
grants.award_text: Up to $20,000 per piece of equipment
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include School Food Authorities (SFAs), public schools, non-public schools, charter schools, and residential childcare programs.
key_requirements: Applicants must be School Food Authorities (SFAs).
Non-public and charter schools must prequalify by the application deadline.
Applications must include mandatory required documents as described in the RFP.
Applications must be submitted via the SharePoint site.
Equipment acquisition cost cannot exceed $20,000 unless the applicant covers the excess cost.

Introduction  
 
The Fiscal Year ( FY) 202 3, Consolidated Appropriations Act  (Public Law 117 -328),  has provided funding in the 
amount of  $30,000,000 to be distributed to State Agencies (SA s) that will competitively award equipment 
assistance grants  to eligible  School  Food  Authorities  (SFA s) participa ting in the National  School  Lunch  Program  
(NSLP) . 
 
These funds will allow SFAs to purchase equipment , with a value of greater than $1,000, needed to serve 
healthier meals ; support scratch cooking; improve the overall quality of meals ; improve  food  safety; and 
expand access  and help to support the establishment, maintenance, or expansion of the School Breakfast 
Program  (SBP) .  
 The equipment purchased with the FY  2023  NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant must be used to support the 
federally assisted sch ool meals programs. Equipment may not be purchased exclusively for programs outside 
of the federally assisted school meals programs.  When a n RA participates in other school meal programs [such 
as the School Breakfast Program (SBP), Afterschool Snack Progra m (ASP), Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program 
(FFVP), Summer Food Service Program (SFSP)], in addition to the NSLP, those other meals programs may benefit from equipment purchased with FY  2023  NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant funds. For example, if a n 
RA participating in the NSLP and SBP purchases a new refrigerator with the FY 2023  NSLP  Equipment  Assistance  
Grant  funds,  food  items  for both  federal programs  may  be stored  in the refrigerator.  
 The SFA will apply on behalf of their eligible Recipient Agencies ( RAs). Unless otherwise exempt, as detailed 
in this R equest for P roposals (RFP),  the SFA will submit a separate application for each piece of requested 
equipment for an eligible RA.   
 
This p roject has been funded at least in part with f ederal funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The 
contents of this publication do not necessarily reflect the view or policies of the U.S. Department of Agriculture,  
nor does  mention  of trade  names,  commercial  products,  or organizations  imply  endorsement by the U.S.  
Government.

funding must return any unobligated funds to NYSED by no later than January 15, 2025. All procurement 
and expenditure activities mus t be completed no later than 6/30/ 2025 .

All SFAs  are eligible to apply for funding for their RAs  that participate in the  NSLP, including public school 
districts, non -profit nonpublic schools, charter schools and residential childcare institutions  in New York State.

Workers’ Compensation Coverage and Debarment  
 
New York State Workers’ Compensation Law (WCL) has specific coverage requirements for businesses 
contracting with New York State and addi tional requirements that provide for the debarment of vendors that 
violate certain sections of WCL. The WCL requires, and has required since introduction of the law in 1922, the 
heads of all municipal and State entities to ensure that businesses have appro priate workers’ compensation 
and disability benefits insurance coverage prior  to issuing any permits or licenses, or prior  to entering into 
contracts.  
 
Workers’ compensation requirements are covered by WCL Section 57, while disability benefits are covered by 
WCL Section 220(8). The Workers’ Compensation Benefits clause in Appendix A –  STANDARD CLAUSES FOR 
NEW YORK STATE CONTRACTS states that in accordance with Section 142 of the State Finance Law, a contract 
shall be void and of no force and effect unless the contractor provides and maintains coverage during the life 
of the contract for the benefit of such employees as are required to be covered by the provisions of the WCL.  
 Under provisions of the 2007 Workers’ Compensation Reform Legislation (WCL Section 141 -b), any person, or 
entity substantially owned by that person: subject to a final assessment of civil fines or penalties, subject to a stop -work order, or convicted of a misdemeanor for violation of Workers’ Compensation laws Section 52 or 
131, is barred from bidding on, or being awarded, any public work contract or subcontract with the State, any 
municipal corporation or public body for one year for each violation. The ban is five years for each felony conviction.  
PROOF OF COVERAGE REQUIREMENTS   
The Workers’ Compensation Board has developed several forms to assist State contracting entities in ensuring 
that businesses have the appropriate workers’ compensation and disability insurance coverage as required by Sections 57 and 220(8) of the WCL.  
 Please note – an ACORD form is not acceptable proof of New York State workers’ compensation or disability 
benefits insurance coverage .

Focus of SFA Grants  
 
The equipment request and grant application submission must address how the equipment improves the 
qual ity of school meals.  
 
The application will also address one  focus area from the following: 
 
• Focus 1: Food  Safety  
 
Equipment that improves the safety of food served in the school nutrition programs (e.g., cold/hot holding 
equipment, dishwashing equipment, refrigeration, milk coolers, freezers, blast chillers, etc.)  
 
• Focus 2: Serving Healthier School  Meals  
 
Equipment that allows for preparing, cooking , and serving healthier school meals , scratch cooking  and 
increasing nutritional quality (e.g., salad bars,  storage of fresh food,  steaming equipment, refrigeration units).  
 
• Focus 3: Expanded Participation  in NSLP and/or SBP  
 
Equipment that allows SFAs to support expanded participation in the NSLP  and/or SBP (e.g., equipment for 
serving meals in a non -traditional setting or to better utilize cafeteria space  or equipment that will help to 
support the establishment, maintenance, or expansion of the SBP .) 
 
Equipment Requests  
 Regulations at 2 CFR Part 200.33 define equipment as tangible personal property, having a useful life of more 
than one year and a per -unit acquisition cost which equals or exceeds the lesser of the capitalization level 
established by the non -Federal entity  for financial statement purposes, or $5,000 per unit. However, for the 
FY 2023 NSLP Equipment Assistance Grant, Congress has specified that the threshold for the purchase of 
equipment has been lowered to $1,000.  This definition will be used for purposes of this grant and recording 
of equipment costs.  
 
Equipment requests may include new equipment, used equipment, and replacement of equipment with a per 
item acquisition cost greater than $1,000 . This grant does not  apply to equipment that has already been 
purchased.  SFAs may receive up to $20,000 in equipment for each eligible RA.  
 
Multiple items whose per -unit acquisition cost is less than $1,000 may not be combined to meet the minimum 
value of greater than $1,000 . 
 
Under no circumstance will a grant be awarded for an item that does not  have an acquisition  cost greater than  
$1,000.  
  

   
 
 11 Grant funding may not be used to purchase items that are used solely for the sale of a la carte products.  
 
As with all federal funds,  the equipment purchases must be necessary, reasonable, and allocable. Using these 
funds to purchase a walk -in freezer for school nutrition programs is an allowable cost; however, renovation of 
the school nutrition area would fall under the category of con struction costs, which  must be charged to the 
school general fund or capital outlay fund . 
 
New York State must comply with the statutory requirement that grants are to be based on the need for 
equipment assistance in participating RAs.  
 
SFAs should consider and address the following factors, as applicable, when answering the grant application questions:  
• How the equipment will benefit the  school meals programs including contribution to improving 
quality of school  meals  
• The availability of existing State and Local funding for equipment purchases  
• Age of current food service  equipment o r lack of appropriate items  
• Strategies for adopting cafeteria changes that provide more convenience and appeal to the student  
• Opportunities to realize a meaningful impact on nutrition and quality of  school meals  
 
Acquisition Cost  
 
Acquisition  cost is defined  as the net invoice  unit price  of the property,  including the cost of modifications, 
attachments, accessories, or auxiliary apparatus necessary to make the property usable for the purpose for  
which  it was acquired.  Other  charges  such  as the cost of installation,  transportation,  duty  or protective in -transit 
insurance, shall be included or excluded from the unit acquisition cost in accordance with the grantee’s regular 
accounting practices. The cost of building renovation or construction of school nutrition areas are not included 
under acquisition costs.

TARGETED  SUPPORT FOR LONG -TERM IDENTIFIED SCHOOLS Grant  
i 
 Project Purpose  
For the 20 23-24 school year, the New York State Education Department (NYSED or “the 
Department”) is providing Target Districts with schools in the Receivership support model 
that participate in the Targeted Coaching the opportunity to receive additional support 
and technical assistance to assist these schools in meeting their annual identified targets.    
 
Title I School Improvement Grant 1003 TARGETED  SUPPORT  FOR LONG -TERM 
IDENTIFIED SCHOOLS  funds will be provided to support these schools .  These funds 
will be separate from the Title I School Improvement Grant 1003 BASIC funds  that districts 
are currently using to advance their improvement initiatives.   
 
Eligibility 
Target Districts  that have  at least one school  in the Receivership program  that has 
registered for Targeted Coaching are eligible to submit applications for this grant . 
 
A full list of eligible schools can be found in Attachment B  – SIG TARGETED  SUPPORT  
Eligible Schools.  
 
Fund ing 
The Department is providing $ 125,000 per eligible school.  
 
Allowable Uses of Funds  
The Department has established guidance and parameters for districts regarding the use 
of these funds:  
 
1. The funds must directly connect to the 202 3-24 Continuation Plan for all eligible 
Receivership schools.  
 
2. The funds must support activities and expenses that will contribute to success with the Demonstrable Improvement Indicators  (DIIs) / Lead Strategies.   
 
Principals will work with their District  to complete a School Spending Plan for each 
eligible school as part of a single LEA application.  Districts should ensure that the 
submitted school spending plans align with the Demonstrable Improvement Indicators  
(DIIs) / Lead Strategies identified in the school Continuation P lans.  
As part of the application review, NYSED will be looking for alignment between 
Continuation  Plans, Spending Plans, and the FS -10 budget costs.  
 Please refer to Attachment A for examples of how to complete the Spending Plan . 
 
Due to the size of these grants, the Department will support districts that choose to pay 
for staff positions with these funds, provided these staff positions directly connect to 
established DIIs  / Lead Strategies .  Any staff positions  funded through this program must

ii 
 comply with federal “supplement, not supplant” guidelines and should not include  core 
instructional positions.   
 
SIG TARGETED SUPPORT  funds cannot be used to support schools within the district 
that are not listed in Attachment B  as an eligible school.  If the district wishes to fund an 
expense that would support eligible and non- eligible schools, SIG TARGETED 
SUPPORT  funds could only be used for the portion that will go toward eligible schools.  
The remaining amount for the portion that will support non- eligible schools must be 
covered by a different funding s ource .   
 
Project Period  
September  1, 202 3 to August 31, 202 4 
 
Application Dea dline  
Completed applications are due by October 14, 2023,  and will be reviewed on a rolling 
basis. LEAs are encouraged to submit completed applications as soon as possible to 
expedite the review and approval process . 
 
Submission Instructions  
To receive SIG TARGETED SUPPORT  funding, eligible Districts must  submit : 
 
1. the blue ink signed Application Cover Page  
2. a School Spending Plan for each participating school  
3. one signed original and two hard copies of the District’s FS-10 budget form   
4. the 202 3-24 Continuation Plan for each participating Receivership school  
 
LEAs are required to send the s ubmission documents listed above to: 
 NYS Education Department -  Office of Accountability

Albany, New York 12234

.

grants.summary: This grant provides funding to eligible New York State school districts to continue High School Redesign efforts for schools in CSI, ATSI, or TSI support models.
grants.description: The New York State Education Department offers funding to Target Districts with schools in the CSI, ATSI, or TSI support models that participated in the 2022-23 High School Redesign Program. The grant supports activities such as convening High School Redesign teams, implementing High School Redesign Plans (HSRP) or School Comprehensive Education Plans (SCEP), and aligning spending plans with these initiatives. Applications must include specific documentation and be submitted both in hard copy and electronically.
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants are Target Districts with at least one school in the CSI, ATSI, or TSI model that participated in the 2022-23 High School Redesign Program.
key_requirements: Applicant must be a Target District in New York State.
At least one school in the district must be in the CSI, ATSI, or TSI model.
The school must have participated in the 2022-23 High School Redesign Program.
Submission must include a School Spending Plan, HSRP or SCEP, and FS-10 budget form.
Applications must be submitted both in hard copy and electronically.

High School Redesign (HSR)  Continuation 
i 
  
Project Purpose  
For the 20 23-24 school year, the New York State Education Department (NYSED or “the 
Department”) is providing Target Districts with schools  in the CSI, ATSI, or TSI support 
models that participated in the 2022- 23 High School Redesign P rogram with the 
opportunity to receive School  Improvement Grant 1003 High School Redesign 
Continuation funds to continue their implementation efforts .   
 
These funds will be separate from the Title I School Improvement Grant 1003 BASIC 
funds that districts are currently using to advance district -level and school -level 
improvement initiatives . 
 
Eligibility 
Target Districts with at least one school  in the CSI, ATSI, or TSI model  that participated 
in the High School Redesign support model in 202 2-23 are eligible to submit an 
application for 2023-24 SIG High School Redesign  Continuation  funding .  A full list of 
schools that meet these criteria can be found in A ttachment C. 
Funding  
The Department will provide  eligible districts with $ 100,000  in funding per school to 
support allowable activities associated with the continuation of the school’s High School 
Redesign.   
 
Allowable Uses of Funds  
The funds must be used to advance High School Redesign activities  at eligible  
participating school s by supporting the expenses  associated with the convening of the 
school’s established High School Redesign team , supporting the implementation of the 
school’s 2023- 24 High School Redesign Plan (HSRP )/School Comprehensive 
Education Plan (SCEP) . 
High School Redesign Teams will work with their District to complete a School Spending 
Plan for each eligible school as part of a single LEA application.   Districts should ensure 
that the submitted school spending plans align with the 2023- 24 HSRP or, for schools 
that an SCEP in lieu of an HSRP, the 2023- 24 SCEP.    
 As part of the application review, NYSED will be looking for alignment between the SCEPs  
OR HSRPs,  Spending Plans, and the FS -10 budget  costs . 
  Please refer to Attachment B for examples of potential SIG H igh School  Redesign 
Expenses.  
 Due to the size of these grants, the Department will support districts that choose to pay 
for staff positions with these funds, provided the staff positions directly support  the HSRP 
or SCEP .  Any staff position funded through this program must comply with federal 
“supplement, not supplant” guidelines and may not be used to fund core instructional

ii 
 positions.  The Department does not envision  offering High School Redesign Continuation  
funding following the 2023- 24 school year.  Districts should plan accordingly.  
 
Please refer to Attachment A for an example of how to complete the application.  
 
Project Period  
September  1, 202 3 to August 31, 202 4 
 
Application Deadline  
Completed a pplications, including the corresponding School Spending Plans , 
are due by September 29, 2023,  and will be reviewed on a rolling basis. LEAs are 
encouraged to submit completed applications as soon as possible to expedite the review 
and approval process.  
 
Submission Instructions  
To receive SIG High School Redesign Continuation  funding, eligible Districts must  submit  
one signed original and two copies of :
